title: Deployment Strategies and Operational Rollback
description: Personalized DOP-C02 training for selecting deployment strategies from operational constraints; CodeDeploy lifecycle, load balancer, alarm, rollback, and Auto Scaling behavior; Lambda alias traffic shifting with hooks and alarms; and Elastic Beanstalk rolling, immutable, and traffic-splitting deployments.

topicDescriptors.title: Choose the Deployment Strategy from Operational Constraints
CodeDeploy Operational Flow, Hooks, Load Balancers, and Rollback
Lambda Aliases, Traffic Shifting, Validation Hooks, and Alarms
Elastic Beanstalk Rolling, Immutable, and Traffic-Splitting Deployments

conceptMaps.title: Choose a deployment strategy from constraints, not service names

steps.label: 1. Availability
steps.detail: Decide whether any capacity loss or downtime is acceptable. All-at-once is immediately eliminated when availability must be preserved.

steps.label: 2. Extra capacity
steps.detail: Ask whether the solution may launch a parallel fleet or extra batch. Blue/green and immutable trade additional capacity for isolation and safer rollback.

steps.label: 3. Traffic control
steps.detail: Identify whether traffic must move all at once, by percentage, or only after a test window and approval.

steps.label: 4. Rollback mechanism
steps.detail: Prefer a strategy whose rollback directly matches the failure signal: target health, lifecycle hook failure, or CloudWatch alarm.

steps.label: 5. Platform scope
steps.detail: Separate an application-version deployment from an environment replacement, configuration update, or Lambda alias shift.

steps.label: 1. Provision replacement
steps.detail: Create or identify the green instances with the intended launch configuration and application revision.

steps.label: 2. Install and start
steps.detail: Run the configured EC2 lifecycle scripts and validate the application before production traffic.

steps.label: 3. Register with target group
steps.detail: The load balancer health check must succeed before traffic can be safely routed.

steps.label: 4. Shift traffic
steps.detail: CodeDeploy reroutes production traffic to the replacement environment according to the deployment configuration.

steps.label: 5. Observe and roll back
steps.detail: Deployment failures or configured CloudWatch alarms can trigger automatic rollback to the last known good revision.

steps.label: 6. Retire blue
steps.detail: Keep or terminate the original instances after the configured wait period.

steps.label: 1. Publish immutable version
steps.detail: A deployment targets a published Lambda version, not mutable $LATEST.

steps.label: 2. Run pre-traffic validation
steps.detail: Use a pre-traffic or BeforeAllowTraffic validation when a prerequisite must complete before any production traffic reaches the new version.

steps.label: 3. Shift alias traffic
steps.detail: CodeDeploy changes alias weights using canary, linear, or all-at-once behavior.

steps.label: 4. Observe alarms
steps.detail: CloudWatch alarms can stop the deployment and trigger rollback while traffic is shifting.

steps.label: 5. Run post-traffic validation
steps.detail: Use post-traffic validation for checks that require the new version to be serving production traffic.

conceptMaps.title: Elastic Beanstalk deployment policy decision tree

steps.label: Can downtime occur?
steps.detail: All at once is the fastest and cheapest but removes all serving capacity during deployment.

steps.label: Update existing instances?
steps.detail: Rolling updates batches of existing instances. Rolling with additional batch temporarily preserves full capacity.

steps.label: Need isolated new instances?
steps.detail: Immutable launches a full new Auto Scaling group and provides safer rollback by terminating the new group if deployment fails.

steps.label: Need production canary traffic?
steps.detail: Traffic splitting launches new instances and sends a configured percentage of traffic for an evaluation period.

steps.label: Need separate environment ownership?
steps.detail: Blue/green uses a second environment and swaps CNAMEs, which is different from an in-environment deployment policy.

steps.label: 1. Choose the signal
steps.detail: Use application lifecycle validation, load balancer health, or a CloudWatch alarm that represents user impact.

steps.label: 2. Attach it to the deployment group
steps.detail: The signal must be configured where CodeDeploy can consume it; a metric without an alarm is not enough.

steps.label: 3. Enable automatic rollback
steps.detail: Configure rollback for failed deployments and/or alarm threshold breaches.

steps.label: 4. Verify last known good revision
steps.detail: CodeDeploy rollback creates a new deployment of the previously known good revision.

drillDefinitions.title: Constraint-to-strategy sentence
drillDefinitions.instructions: Read the mechanism and identify the tradeoff before naming a service.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Deployment choice is a constraint-matching problem: availability, extra capacity, traffic-control granularity, rollback speed, and resource scope determine the strategy.

explanation.concise: La estrategia se elige por restricciones operativas, no por el nombre del servicio.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Esta secuencia elimina opciones que son técnicamente posibles pero no cumplen el costo, el tiempo de prueba o el alcance.

drillDefinitions.title: Rolling or blue/green?
drillDefinitions.instructions: Choose the mechanism that matches the requirement.
drillDefinitions.prompt: A production team must keep the original fleet untouched for two hours, test a full-capacity replacement fleet, then shift traffic and automatically terminate the original fleet. Which strategy fits?

answerOptions.label: Rolling deployment
Blue/green deployment

distractorMetadata.failure: Rolling modifica la flota existente por lotes; no conserva una flota azul completa e intacta durante dos horas.

explanation.concise: El requisito pide dos flotas simultáneas y una transferencia explícita de tráfico.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Blue/green crea el entorno de reemplazo y conserva el original durante la validación.

distractorReview.failure: Rolling modifica la flota existente por lotes; no conserva una flota azul completa e intacta durante dos horas.

drillDefinitions.title: Map constraints to deployment mechanisms
drillDefinitions.instructions: Map each requirement ID to the best strategy ID.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Match each operational requirement to its deployment strategy.

mappingItems.label: Deploy only to a new full set of instances with quick rollback
Send a percentage of real traffic for an evaluation period
Keep a complete original environment while testing a replacement

explanation.concise: Cada estrategia tiene una señal decisiva distinta.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: El mapa obliga a traducir requisitos operativos a mecanismos antes de considerar servicios.

drillDefinitions.title: Eliminate the almost-correct deployment
drillDefinitions.instructions: Select the BEST answer, not merely an available strategy.
drillDefinitions.prompt: An EC2 application behind an ALB needs a full replacement fleet, zero downtime, a two-hour validation window, traffic cutover after approval, and automatic termination of the old fleet. What is the BEST design?

answerOptions.label: Elastic Beanstalk rolling update with 20% batches
CodeDeploy blue/green and terminate original instances after a two-hour wait
CodeDeploy in-place OneAtATime deployment
Create a second environment manually and delete the first immediately after DNS change

distractorMetadata.attraction: Rolling conserva disponibilidad y parece menos costoso.
distractorMetadata.failure: No crea una flota paralela completa ni conserva la original intacta.
Es in-place y no ofrece la ventana de prueba sobre una flota verde completa.

distractorMetadata.attraction: Una segunda flota manual se parece a blue/green.
distractorMetadata.failure: Añade trabajo manual y no cumple la terminación administrada después de dos horas.

explanation.concise: CodeDeploy blue/green satisface todas las restricciones y configura la espera antes de terminar la flota original.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Es la única opción con flota paralela, cambio de tráfico administrado, ventana de prueba y terminación automática.

distractorReview.attraction: Rolling conserva disponibilidad y parece menos costoso.
distractorReview.failure: No crea una flota paralela completa ni conserva la original intacta.
Es in-place y no ofrece la ventana de prueba sobre una flota verde completa.

distractorReview.attraction: Una segunda flota manual se parece a blue/green.
distractorReview.failure: Añade trabajo manual y no cumple la terminación administrada después de dos horas.

answerOptions.label: Rolling deployment in small batches

drillDefinitions.instructions: Review the distinction without scoring it as an exam answer.
drillDefinitions.prompt: Rolling changes the existing fleet in batches. Blue/green creates a replacement environment and reroutes traffic. Immutable creates a new full fleet inside the environment. Traffic splitting adds percentage-based production canary traffic.

explanation.concise: El repaso separa cuatro mecanismos que suelen sonar equivalentes en opciones largas.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Recordar qué recurso se reemplaza evita elegir por palabras como gradual o zero downtime.

drillDefinitions.title: CodeDeploy EC2 control plane
drillDefinitions.instructions: Trace what CodeDeploy controls and what the ALB validates.
drillDefinitions.prompt: For EC2 deployments, CodeDeploy coordinates the revision, AppSpec lifecycle scripts, deployment group, instance registration or deregistration, traffic routing, alarms, and rollback. The ALB independently reports target health.

explanation.concise: CodeDeploy orquesta el despliegue; el ALB aporta la señal de salud de los targets.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: Separar orquestación de health checks permite diagnosticar AllowTraffic y rollback.

drillDefinitions.title: AllowTraffic failed with no deployment-log error
drillDefinitions.instructions: Choose the most direct root-cause layer.
drillDefinitions.prompt: A blue/green EC2 deployment reaches AllowTraffic, but the replacement targets never become healthy and deployment scripts show no error. Which area should be checked first?

answerOptions.label: ALB target-group health check configuration
The previous deployment ApplicationStop script

distractorMetadata.attraction: Los hooks pueden causar fallos de CodeDeploy.
distractorMetadata.failure: No explica que el fallo ocurra al permitir tráfico mientras los targets permanecen unhealthy.

explanation.concise: AllowTraffic depende de que los targets puedan registrarse y aprobar health checks.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: La señal apunta a la capa de balanceador, no a un script de un despliegue anterior.

distractorReview.attraction: Los hooks pueden causar fallos de CodeDeploy.
distractorReview.failure: No explica que el fallo ocurra al permitir tráfico mientras los targets permanecen unhealthy.

explanation.concise: El flujo separa preparación, validación, tráfico y retiro.

drillDefinitions.title: Successful deployment, mixed application versions
drillDefinitions.instructions: Diagnose the interaction between deployment and scaling.
drillDefinitions.prompt: During an in-place rolling CodeDeploy deployment to an Auto Scaling group, a scale-out event launches two additional instances from an unchanged launch template. CodeDeploy reports success, but the new instances run the old baked application version. What is the MOST likely explanation?

answerOptions.label: The ALB health check automatically restored the old version
Scale-out created instances from the unchanged launch template outside the already selected deployment targets
CloudWatch alarm rollback updated only two instances
ValidateService installs the previous revision on new instances

distractorMetadata.attraction: El ALB decide qué targets reciben tráfico.
distractorMetadata.failure: No instala ni restaura versiones de aplicación.
El escenario declara éxito y no una alarma activada.

distractorMetadata.attraction: ValidateService forma parte del ciclo de vida.
distractorMetadata.failure: Valida el servicio; no instala deliberadamente la revisión anterior.

explanation.concise: Un scale-out puede introducir instancias creadas desde una configuración que todavía contiene la versión anterior.
explanation.correctChoiceWins: CodeDeploy puede completar sobre su conjunto de targets mientras nuevas instancias aparecen desde la plantilla no actualizada.

explanation.correctChoiceWins: La validación bloquea todo tráfico a la nueva versión hasta que Step Functions confirme finalización.
